content:
Homeowners at La Bota Ranch have taken control of their homeowners associations after a fight that began in 2016, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The transfer was discussed at a community meeting on October 18, 2026, attended by District VII Councilmember Vanessa Perez and Mayor Dr. Victor Trevino.

Homeowners organized in 2016 and sued the developers in 2017 over rising dues and fiduciary concerns. A jury found a breach of fiduciary duties in March 2022, and a new homeowner board was appointed on January 19, 2023. Settlement agreements began in February 2026, and a closing on August 20, 2026, transferred common-area property to the homeowner associations, including the community center, park, streets, soccer field, ponds, and guardhouse.

La Bota Ranch was master-planned in 1992. The surrounding area has also seen a 2024 city ordinance restricting large warehouses within 500 feet of schools, parks, or churches, and a November 2025 city purchase of property across from Muller Elementary School, according to the report.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "La Bota Ranch celebrates ‘Independence Day’ as homeowners take control," October 26, 2026
